headline: 5131 BDU Trainees on EOD Course

body.text: In what insiders are already calling "the boldest personnel decision this quarter," 5131 (BD) Unit has confirmed that its latest intake of trainees is now undergoing formal instruction in the defusing of explosive devices, a course that Fish News understands includes both "the theory" and, somewhat alarmingly, "the practical."

The announcement was met with a mixture of pride and quiet dread across MoD Wattleburn, with one training officer describing the group's first attempt at a controlled defusal as "technically successful, in the sense that a building is still standing."

Fish News reached out to 5131 (BD) Unit for comment and received a statement that, true to form, answered none of the questions actually asked: "Every trainee has demonstrated excellent wire discipline, a firm grasp of the manual, and an admirable willingness to let the instructor go first."

One trainee, speaking on the condition of anonymity and at a distance the Fish News' correspondent found reassuring, summarised the course thus: "Red wire, blue wire, and a great deal of hoping." When pressed for further detail, they declined, citing "a strong professional interest in still having fingers."

A senior instructor, when asked how the course was progressing, paused for a length of time Fish News felt was "not entirely encouraging" before replying, "no comment, and please stop asking that particular question."

body.credit: Someone at the Royal Air Force

body.text: Fish News will continue to monitor 5131 (BD) Unit's progress through the course, from what it is assured is a perfectly safe distance.
